title: Introduce SSE-driven RAG orchestrator and typed tool-adapter playground
author: Olivia Chen
release_notes: Adds an SSE-based orchestrator sample for RAG flows, typed tool adapter bindings, a lightweight micro-frontend dev playground, and docs. Opt-in example; no breaking API changes.
description: Motivation: Provide a compact, production-adjacent example that demonstrates how to build a streaming RAG orchestration layer using Server-Sent Events (SSE) for low-overhead client updates and typed tool-binding adapters for predictable tool calls. This PR ships a small playground that: 1) streams retrieval events and partial responses to the browser; 2) exposes a typesafe adapter shim for tool calling (HTTP/webhook, local mock, and typed RPC stubs); 3) integrates telemetry probes for per-step latency and token accounting; and 4) documents a stepwise quickstart for developers. Implementation notes: - Core orchestrator: a minimal Node/Express service that manages RAG sessions and emits SSE events for retrievals, candidate scoring, and generation deltas. The orchestrator is intentionally framework-agnostic and designed to be dropped into examples or extended for serverless runners. - Typed tool adapters: TypeScript adapter interface (ToolAdapter) plus three concrete adapters included: webhook-adapter (outbound HTTP), local-mock-adapter (dev-friendly deterministic responses), and rpc-adapter (tiny JSON-RPC over unix socket for local testing). Adapters provide a runtime contract: name, schema, call(), and a JSON-schema for contract validation used by the sample client to render tool contracts in the micro-frontend. - Micro-frontend: lightweight dev server + React-based UI that opens an SSE connection, visualizes retrieval traces, tool invocations, and incremental model deltas, with interactive buttons to replay or re-run steps with different adapters. - Telemetry: example telemetry probes (step-timing, tokens-emitted, adapter-latency) wired to a logger adapter and optional OTLP exporter in docs. - Docs/Quickstart: single-page quickstart that explains how to run dev mode, switch adapters, wire a Redwood hosted model vs. local model stub, and run smoke e2e. Checklist: - [x] implement SSE orchestrator and session protocol - [x] add typed adapter interface + three adapters - [x] micro-frontend dev playground and hot-reload scripts - [x] example telemetry hooks and sample OTLP/exporter wiring - [x] docs quickstart + API contract examples - [x] unit tests for adapter contract validation - [x] CI smoke e2e against local mock model How to run (short): 1) yarn install && yarn build 2) yarn start:dev (starts orchestrator, mock model, and micro-frontend) 3) open http://localhost:3333 and follow the in-page quickstart to select a tool adapter and run a sample RAG session Security notes: adapters validate tool payloads with JSON-schema; webhook-adapter supports allowlist config and optional HMAC signing header for outbound calls. Production note: this playground is not hardened for multi-tenant production without adding auth, rate limits, and stronger adapter sandboxing. Testing: added unit tests for contract validator and an integration smoke test that runs a short RAG flow against the local-mock-adapter and asserts SSE event ordering. Related: This PR complements ENG-1289 (retrieval/telemetry patterns) and follows the docs patterns used in previous quickstarts but intentionally focuses on streaming UX and typed adapters rather than full orchestration/autoscaling.
